dog.description_text:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.

Pre-Screener Form

Nova Star is at risk due to behavior concerns in the previous home and during her stay in care. In her previous home, Nova Star is reported to have initiated multiple altercations with the other resident dog without clear warnings or triggers, which resulted in bites to both dogs. In care, Nova Star has been struggling to acclimate despite best efforts to keep her comfortable. In quiet, calmer settings, she will approach multiple handlers for pets but quickly becomes overwhelmed and will begin pacing around the room. She intermittently has to be carried out of her crate as she will baulk/pancake in the hallway. Medically, Nova Star has CIRDC and healing wounds.

Nova Star was surrendered by her previous owner due to conflict with the other resident dog in the home. Nova Star's previous family described her as a very affectionate dog who enjoyed playing with balls and squeaky toys, loved vegetables as snacks, and wanted to be anywhere her people were in the home. She is reported to have initiated several altercations with the other resident dog, which has resulted in bites to both dogs that have broken the skin and drawn blood. During her stay in care, Nova Star has been highly fearful and becomes conflicted with handlers when interacting. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.
dog.name: Nova Star
